Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The Sri Lankan players stride out to the middle, followed by Aiden Markram and Janneman Malan. Dushmantha Chameera will start with the ball for the hosts.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

What do we learn from the previous para? Of course, South Africa have a tendency to choke in tournament knockouts. (Remember, this is a series decider). Second, the second essay of that run chase saw Harbhajan Singh and Virender Sehwag take 5 wickets in 13 overs. So it means that you need one set batsman to bat through. And spinners are never out of the game. So even though 204 could seem a smallish total, a spinning track could provide us a wonderful run chase. Please do stay tuned, folks.

Right then. South Africa have 204 to chase but it won't be an easy chase as the pitch will aid spinners. Sri Lanka will need their bowlers to step up and deliver. Flashback - 2002 Champions Trophy - Semifinal between South Africa and India at this very same ground. India made 261/9 in 50 overs, while the Proteas were 192/1 in 37 overs. Then, suddenly, Herschelle Gibbs suffered cramps in his hands and had to retire hurt. What followed next was harakiri. South Africa, needing 70 from 78 balls, with technically 9 wickets in hand, practically 8, lost their way, stumbling to 213/4 and eventually, lost by 10 runs.

One might argue - what is the sense in having Aiden Markram bowl, that too, ahead of Tabraiz Shamsi? Well, Maharaj just trusted his instincts and given that there was a right hand-left hand combination in the middle, with Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva batting, he thought of getting on an offie. That move did not quite work then but Markram did get a wicket later on. And then, Shamsi wove his magic again. Overall, these were the figures of all the spinners combined - 40-1-142-8. Poor Andile Phehlukwayo and Wiaan Mulder got just one over each, that too because there were lack of bowling options ar the death! That explains Mulder's frustration and fury in the 49th over.

South Africa will be pretty pleased with their performance. The bowlers, especially their spinners, were brilliant. How many times to do you see spin opening the innings? That too, from a non-Asian team? We saw that in this innings. Rabada bowled the first over but skipper Keshav Maharaj took the second new ball to himself. He has done it in domestic games for the Dolphins, back in South Africa, when they play on slow pitches in Durban. And he read the pitch to perfection. He struck in his very second over, removing Avishka Fernando and then, realizing that the deck is supporting spinners, got George Linde from the other end. And got rewarded quickly enough. His reading of the game was equally impressive as he overturned two of the on-field umpire's calls to get wickets in his team's favour.

The top order failed to score runs as each of them fell below 20. Avishka Fernando and Dinesh Chandimal both fell to LBW while Mendis's struggle came to end as he chipped one back to Linde. Dhananjaya de Silva put on some resistance alongside Asalanka but eventually perished against Markram. After that, the wickets kept tumbling for Sri Lanka. Asalanka stayed solid in the middle and worked hard for his 47 but he also departed. Chameera played a useful hand of 29 but none of the batters really managed to get going and in the end, SL managed to put 203 on the board.

Eight out of the nine wickets fell to spin and this gives a clear indication about how the pitch is moving and South Africa have done well to exploit the conditions. Dushmantha Chameera and Maheesh Theekshana added 32 runs for the 9th wicket and that helped Sri Lanka cross the 200-run mark and have something to defend with their spinners.

Full on off, Theekshana heaves it to long on. He takes the single but Jayawickrama calls him for the second. The throw comes in to the keeper who behaves casually, as if the throw is not coming to him and then, at the last moment, collects the ball and whips the bails off and appeals for a run out, ala MS Dhoni style. But the square leg umpire is pretty sure that Theekshana has made it in, so it will be two runs to the total. SRI LANKA END ON 203 FOR 9.

BACK IN YOUR CREASE! Oh my, aggression from Mulder. Full on middle, Theekshana plays it back to the bowler. Now, he comes out of the crease in his followthrough but by no means, was he attempting the run. But Mulder picked the ball up and fired a throw back at the striker's end. Poor Theekshana had to rush back into his crease and perhaps the ball hit his back leg, while going through to Heinrich Klaasen. Now, Theekshana seemed to be giving a stare back at Mulder who was going off but then, when he saw the batter giving him a stare, decided to stare back. However, he then received a smile from Theekshana and the matter ended there. Could have been something different if Maheesh had decided to persist with his stare, aye?

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Ho ho ho! Appeal for something, get something else, they say! Not quite sure if the Proteas themselves knew this was out caught. It was a fuller ball, outside off, Charith Asalanka lunged to defend and the ball whizzed past the outside edge. Heinrich Klaasen collected the ball cleanly and whipped the bails off in a flash, and was celebrating the stumping, clearly. He was looking at Asalanka's back foot and then, at the square leg umpire. So clearly, he did not feel that there might have been a nick. The square leg umpire took it upstairs but as is the norm these days, the third umpire checks for everything. So first, the no ball, which is fine. Then, the outside edge. Oh wait. Now, when the ball passes the bat, there is a murmur. It is almost neglectable, but the third umpire seems interested. He checks that to and fro and eventually, is convinced that there was an edge! We don't even get to see whether the foot was dragged out of the crease. End of a fighting knock from Asalanka.
Commentary.Howout: c Heinrich Klaasen b Tabraiz Shamsi

Flighted ball, on leg. Dhananjaya de Silva prods and pushes it to wide of mid off for a single.
On leg, tucked on the leg side for a single.

Loopy ball on leg, turning away. Dhananjaya de Silva looks to flick but gets hit on the pads.
Tossed up, full and on off. Kamindu Mendis steps out and eases it down to long off. He crosses ends.

Beaten! Tossed up ball, outside off. Kamindu Mendis again gets low and looks to sweep. But misses.
Slower through the air, on middle. Kamindu Mendis looks to work it on the leg side but miscues. The ball goes off the outside edge towards point.

Tabraiz Shamsi comes into the attack.

Flatter ball on off, de Silva guides it to first slip where the fielder does well to make a stop.
Powerplay 2 time! 4 fielders can be stationed outside the 30-yard circle now, till the 40th over.
Floated on off, de Silva defends it to point.
Floated on middle, Mendis looks to defend but it goes off the inner half to short fine leg. Sri Lanka are 53 for 2 at the end of Powerplay 1.
Tossed up on middle, de Silva flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Beautifully played! Tossed up on off, de Silva dances down the track and then drives it through mid off for a boundary. 50 up for Sri Lanka.
Full on the pads, Mendis flicks it to deep square leg for one.
Flatter on the pads, de Silva tucks it to square leg for one.
Full on off, de Silva drives it to long off for a single.
Tossed up on off, Mendis plays it to mid off and takes a quick run.
Flighted outside off, Mendis drives it to cover.
Full on the pads, de Silva works it to short fine leg for a single.
Tossed up on off, DdS defends it to cover.

FOUR! Uppish but safe! Flighted ball on middle, de Silva looks to sweep but it goes off the top edge to deep square leg for a boundary.

BEATEN! That's gone with the arm! Floated outside off, de Silva looks to flick but misses.

Aiden Markram comes into the attack.
Loopy ball on middle, de Silva defends it to the off side. A brilliant over from George Linde comes to an end.
Floated on off, de Silva pushes it to point.
Flighted on off, de Silva is solid in his defense.
Floated on off, de Silva defends it to cover.
Dhananjaya de Silva is the new batsman in.

South Africa have taken a review for an LBW. UltraEdge shows there is no bat involved. Ball Tracker shows all three reds. Another brilliant review from South Africa. The on-field decision will be overturned.

OUT! LBW! What a review from South Africa! They have been perfect with their reviews so far! Brilliant stuff. Floated on middle and leg, Chandimal looks to sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is an appeal made for LBW, but there is no conviction in it. Linde himself is not too sure and is pretty much happy to go back and bowl but Keshav Maharaj, don't know from where, is pretty confident that this is plumb. He takes the review straightaway and voila! Ball Tracker shows all three reds and South Africa have their second! Perhaps Linde thought that was pitching outside leg, but Maharaj was supremely confident.
Tossed up on off, Chandimal pushes it back to the bowler.
George Linde comes into the attack.
Flatter on middle, Mendis works it to mid-wicket.
On off, pushed to point.
How did that miss the stumps? Flatter ball on off, it spins. Mendis looks to flick but seems to have missed. Maharaj appeals for a caught behind but the umpire says no.
Full on off, Mendis defends it to cover.
Full toss on middle and leg, Chandimal clips it to the leg side for a single.
Floated on off, Chandimal blocks it to point.

FOUR! This is so elegant! Full ball outside off, Mendis drives it through cover for a boundary.
FOUR! Nicely done! Back-of-a-length ball down the leg side, Mendis flicks it to fine leg for a boundary.
Good-length ball outside off, Mendis lets it go.
Full outside off, Mendis leaves it alone.

NO BALL! Outside off, left alone. No Ball given as Rabada has overstepped.. A Free Hit will follow.
Kamindu Mendis walks out to bat at No.3.
DRS time! South Africa have taken a review for an LBW. UltraEdge shows there is a flat line as the ball passes the bat. Ball Tracker shows all three reds. The on-field decision will be reversed.

OUT! LBW! Flatter and quicker ball on middle and leg, Avishka Fernando looks to work it on the leg side but misses. He gets pinged on the pads. Keshav Maharaj appeals for an LBW but the umpire says no. South Africa opt for a review. UltraEdge shows there is no bat involved. Ball Tracker shows all three reds. The on-field decision will be reversed. Keshav Maharaj draws first blood and Avishka Fernando has to walk back to the pavillion.
FOUR! Top shot by Fernando! Tossed up on middle and leg, Fernando goes on his knees and then sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Quicker ball on middle, Fernando defends it back to the bowler.
Loopy ball outside off, Fernando lifts it over the point fielder for a couple of runs.
Flatter ball on off, Avishka plays it to cover.
Floated ball on off, Chandimal pushes it to long off for one.
Good-length ball on off, Fernando defends it out.
On off, pushed to point.
Fullish ball on off, Fernando defends it to cover.
FOUR! Punched away! On a length outside off, Fernando punches it through cover-point for a boundary.
Good-length ball on the pads, Chandimal works it wide of mid on for one.
FOUR! Lovely drive! Full on middle, Chandimal leans and drives it past the bowler for a boundary.
Floated on off, Fernando defends it to the off side.
What happened there? That spun a mile! Floated around off, it spun away a lot. Fernando looks to defend but fails to get any bat on it.
BEATEN! Beautifully bowled by Maharaj! Tossed up around off, Fernando looks to defend but gets beaten.
Loopy ball on the pads, Chandimal works it to square leg for a single.

Keshav Maharaj to bowl from the other end.
WIDE! Good-length ball down the leg side, Fernando misses his flick. Wide signalled.
BEATEN! Lovely stuff from Rabada! Full outside off, Fernando looks to drive but misses.
Good-length ball outside off, Fernando pushes it to cover.
WIDE! Full and down the leg side, Fernando looks to flick but misses. Wided.
WIDE! Short ball down the leg side, Fernando looks to pull but misses. Wided.
Sri Lanka are underway! Full on the pads, Fernando looks to flick but it goes off the pads to fine leg for two leg byes.
Good-length ball on off, Fernando pushes it to point off the back foot.
Rabada starts with a good-length ball on middle, Fernando defends it back to the bowler.
Keshav Maharaj, the South African skipper, is up for a chat. He says that it is hot and humid here so they need to save their energy. Informs that they are unchanged.
We are set to begin! South Africa players make their way in the middle. Avishka Fernando and Dinesh Chandimal are the openers for Sri Lanka. Kagiso Rabada to start the proceedings with the ball.

Dasun Shanaka, the Sri Lankan skipper, says that they will bat first. Mentions that hopefully they win this match as the wicket looks good. Informs that their bowling is more important as they didn't bowl well in the last game. Adds that they have made three changes.

Pitch report - Aamir Sohail says the pitch looks hard and well rolled. Mentions that the ball will come onto the bat. Informs that spinners will get assistance from the pitch and they will get turn. Tells that the batters will have to play the spinners well.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Avishka Fernando, Dinesh Chandimal (WK) (IN PLACE OF MINOD BHANUKA), Dhananjaya de Silva, Charith Asalanka, Dasun Shanaka (C), Wanindu Hasaranga, Chamika Karunaratne, Dushmantha Chameera, Kamindu Mendis (IN PLACE OF AKILA DANANJAYA), Praveen Jayawickrama, Maheesh Theekshana (IN PLACE OF BHANUKA RAJAPAKSA) (ODI DEBUT).

South Africa (Unchanged Playing XI) - Janneman Malan, Aiden Markram, Reeza Hendricks, Rassie van der Dussen, Heinrich Klaasen (WK), Andile Phehlukwayo, Wiaan Mulder, George Linde, Keshav Maharaj (C), Kagiso Rabada, Tabraiz Shamsi.
Toss - Sri Lanka have won the toss and they have elected to bat first.

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, would be disappointed with their performance in the second ODI. They do not have a good record in series deciders in the last 7 years and they would want to change that fact in this game. They did well in the first ODI before being hammered in the second game and this is a game which both teams will be looking forward to as it is the decider. Who will come out on top?

South Africa made a strong comeback in the second ODI and lived to fight despite the absence from their ranks of Quinton de Kock, David Miller, and Lungi Ngidi and also without their skipper, Temba Bavuma who had his thumb broken in the first ODI. They face yet another challenge coming into the final ODI as Rabada is a doubt for the match and if he is declared unfit, it will be interesting to see who will replace him.

Hello and welcome to the third and final ODI between Sri Lanka and South Africa. The hosts won the first ODI by 14 runs and then the Proteas stormed back in the second ODI and hammered the Lankan side to level the series 1-1. And here we are, on the cusp of another decider. So the series is even stevens and there is everything to play for in the decider. Who will land the knockout punch? We will find out. Stay tuned for further updates.
